items.title: Dalton Richards Interview, 1961-03-16
items.q: Now, he was with us on that job up there at St. Francisville.

ctx.x: He's a good trombone player. He's a Dixieland trombone player. And, uh, we had Sidney Montague on drums, Howard Davis on trumpet, I mean on saxophone, alto sax and clarinet, Alvin Alcorn on trumpet, Alvin Alcorn was playing, would play banjo and guitar. See? When he played those Dixieland jobs, he used his banjo. And he really could sing, see? So, I mean, at that time I began liking it. One time we went to one of Celestan's jobs, he couldn't fulfill the engagement, so he asked Albert to take charge. We went to…
Oh, I see. Sure boy, is his name Worthy Thomas? Worthy Thomas. That's it, Worthy Thomas. I couldn't think of that. You sure know, he doesn't Worthy Thomas. That's it.

Took me a long time to think of it. Yeah. Now, he was with us on that job up there at St. Francisville. Yeah. And, I mean, we, we just kept on going from place to place like that, until I started getting jobs when I got around two lanes. See, I used to play the twelve hundred Broadway. That's Sigma 58. Fraternity, yeah. Yeah. The Delta Fire on the 25-14 state. 1471, Henry Clay. 1036, Ottomans. 1018, Ottomans. Ten... What did you do? 800 Ottomans. I can't think of all the names.
